description: The figure is a two-ring donut pie chart showing the distribution of response outcomes across two ambiguity levels, with the outer ring representing “Ambiguity 1” and the inner ring representing “Ambiguity 2,” and each ring divided into three categories (three slices per ring). In the outer ring (Ambiguity 1), the slices are labeled Deceived in dark red at 67.6%, Partially in yellow at 23.5%, and Not Deceived in dark green at 8.8%. In the inner ring (Ambiguity 2), the slices are labeled Deceived in bright red at 57.9%, Partially in yellow at 31.6%, and Not Deceived in light green at 10.5%. Percentage labels are printed directly on the slices, and two legends appear on the right—one titled “Ambiguity 1 (Outer)” and one titled “Ambiguity 2 (Inner)”—mapping colors to the three labels; no slices appear exploded or otherwise emphasized, and the segments in both rings appear arranged in the same category order around the circle.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of responses across two levels of ambiguity, labeled as Ambiguity 1 (Outer) and Ambiguity 2 (Inner). For Ambiguity 1, the majority of responses fall under 'Deceived' at approximately 70%, followed by 'Partially' at 20%, and 'Not Deceived' at 10%. For Ambiguity 2, the 'Deceived' category shows a significant decline to 50%, while 'Partially' increases to 40%, and 'Not Deceived' remains stable at 10%. The chart highlights a notable shift in responses between the two levels of ambiguity, with a marked increase in partial deception and a decrease in full deception.
